I'm a director at a large company, a few things I'd recommend from my own experience in identifying potential within employees. Note, these should only be considered if your in it for career development and to get promoted etc, rather than just trucking along at work.

  1. Take a pen and notepad to every meeting. Bring notepad or folio case on day one and your own supplies. You're not a waiter, nobody will be impressed if you remember everything without writing it down, they'll just be concerned you won't follow through on tasks.

  2. Teach yourself to fish where possible, google to look for solutions before bringing in others, and qualify what you have done before attempting to elicit help.

  3. ASK FOR HELP! If you're sticking and have explored other options, there Is nothing worse for a manager than hearing someone say "I couldn't figure this out so I stopped"

  4. Be prepared to review what you have been working on. Usually this means taking notes, and where possible taking initiative. Identify opportunities for for the company (ex: If training material seems poor for something you are tasked to learn, write some!)

  5. Don't whine, find solutions not problems. Package the solutions and "sell then" where appropriate, this is the best form of self promotion and will help your career prospects within the business.

Good luck!
